lastReview.reason: Indirect US-Iran talks in New York produced a concrete Iranian plan to reopen Hormuz. Trump rejected it but says talks resume this week, replacing the 'stalled' picture. Reporting also points to a lower strike tempo, with Trump non-committal on restarting strikes after the midterms. A suspected plot near RAF Fairford is under investigation for possible Iran links.

The Trump-Xi summit in Washington is the main event, but it produced no public Taiwan outcome. Taiwan was reportedly discussed only in private [12], and Xi reportedly pressed Trump to shift his stance on US support for Taiwan and Japan [13]. The ambassador's account that Trump offered Xi arms sales is disputed by Trump himself [8][9], so there is no confirmed change in US policy or deterrence signaling. Commentary on abandonment is balanced by assessments that substantive US capability investment continues [18]. The one-day report of 3 aircraft and 6 vessels [1] is a single data point, not a demonstrated change in tempo. Other items fit the existing gray-zone normalization picture (H1) and do not shift the hypothesis weights: stepped-up PLA activity east of Taiwan [21], Chinese threats of 'consequences' at the Pacific Islands Forum [15], cognitive-domain pressure [16], and Taiwan's multisystem resilience drill [19]. Watch the US deterrence linchpin for any concrete policy follow-through from the summit.

lastReview.reason: Several outlets report renewed large-scale fighting in northern Ethiopia. A Tigray-led coalition of seven armed groups seeks to oust Abiy Ahmed, and fighting has spread across multiple fronts into Afar and Amhara. The UN reports humanitarian operations disrupted. Addis accuses unnamed outside forces of backing the rebels. This is a clear escalation that raises the risk of interstate spillover.

The new reporting fits the current picture and does not shift it. The Rakhine airstrike [1] and the reported bombing from paragliders and gyrocopters [3] match the existing line on continued junta airstrikes on civilian areas. The latter is a change in method, not in tempo or outcome. The Arakan Army's reported control of the full Bangladesh border [6] extends known resistance gains in Rakhine. Its cross-border activity comes from a single outlet and is not yet corroborated. Malaysia's Rohingya deportation plan [4] is a proposal under civil-society pressure, not an implemented action. The junta's regional re-engagement effort [2] and the atrocity-accountability commentary [5] are context, not new developments. No ceasefire, leadership change, major front collapse or shift in China's posture is reported. The assessment stands.

Both moves point to a harder, US-aligned security posture and a move away from total-peace protections. No new kinetic, territorial or humanitarian data were reported, so the STI and sub-scores stay unchanged. The UN restorative-justice note and the InSight Crime ACSN profile are background.

No new kinetic, ceasefire, or implementation development is reported. The UN Security Council briefing says the Gaza plan has stalled and West Bank tensions are rising [6], which matches the current assessment. Axios reports a six-month, $2.45 billion Board of Peace recovery plan [15]. It is a single-outlet scoop about an unveiling, not funded or implemented reconstruction, and the existing 'reconstruction financing as leverage' framing already covers it. Israel's 27 October election, polling as a dead heat [5], is relevant to the coalition linchpin but has not yet changed policy. Netanyahu's UAE visit and the Oct. 7 warning reports [1][4][12] are domestic political context. The remaining items are commentary or peripheral diplomacy. Revisit if the election result shifts Israel's position on implementation, or if recovery funds actually begin to move.
